_doc: Every game system PalCraft touches. One row = one system. owner = which game decides; channels refers to channels.json; code = the file that implements the row ('-' = none in this version).
rows: ReceiveTick hook runs the bridge each frame
CameraActor view target follows Control pose
clears one of 16 tiny render targets per tick
draws world, hand and HUD layers at Present
finds the scene depth buffer for occlusion
hidden character is carried to Steve, held still
line traces answer rays; hills solid from outside
lists nearby Pals with position, box, HP
CombatBridge queues sword, arrow, TNT hits
counts deaths and respawns both ways
F8 in Palworld asks Minecraft to take over
Overlay window glued over the Palworld one
gives kit.json once per player; newer kit waves top up an older kit
reports which parts came alive in a Melty test
mutes the system-info library's warnings about Windows counters
lifts Steve out when terrain fills in around him
names the surface one ray hits: soil, grass, stone, wood, sand, snow or ore
holding attack on Palworld's world digs it: drops by surface and tool
a Pal that Steve kills drops meat, hide, bones and XP; an alpha drops an enchanted golden apple
keeps its mouse pointer hidden while Minecraft holds the mouse
sends the sharpest layers that keep Minecraft above frame_min_fps
takes Steve's food as its stomach and his fires as heat sources; reports body temperature
sends food level and nearby warmth once a second
temperature gauge above the hunger bar, frost on the screen when cold; the bundled AppleSkin draws saturation
finds fire, torches, water and ice around Steve; leather armor counts as warmth
a Pal's hit goes through Minecraft's armor, toughness, Protection and shield rules and wears the armor; cold, heat and poison go past armor as in Minecraft
the old recipe is back: eight gold blocks around an apple make an enchanted golden apple
saves the PalCraft world every autosave_s seconds and the moment Palworld goes away, because the launcher may stop Minecraft without asking
in Palworld mode its own camera leads, shown a few frames late so Minecraft can match it; the character stays hidden
draws Steve where the character stands, walking with it; Steve takes no Minecraft damage meanwhile
a Pal that Steve's hit kills gives the Palworld character experience by its level; reports level and experience earned
shows the experience above the hotbar and a level-up message
